steps.body: A record keeps EVERYTHING: every measurement, repeats included, in the order they came — the raw material of every graph to come.
steps.narration: A record keeps EVERYTHING: every measurement, repeats included, in the order they came — the raw material of every graph to come.

widget.prompt: Record the counts so far as tallies: 6 cm seen 3 times, 7 cm twice, 8 cm once.
widget.successFeedback: Three, two, one — every measurement remembered, repeats and all.
widget.partialFeedback: Match each tally group to how many times that measurement appeared — repeats each earn a mark.

predict.prompt: Your record drops the repeated 6s. What is lost?
predict.reveal: The value 6 survives, but its three-ness dies — and frequency is what the plot will need.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2g record.
invariants: A display and its data are the same information in two forms: every measurement appears exactly once, and counts survive the trip into stacks, rows, and bars for g2g record.
misconceptions: Reading a label as a count, dropping repeats while recording, or comparing categories by adding instead of finding the gap.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change to the data would the display be FORCED to show — and what change could it silently hide?

widget.prompt: You measured five ribbons: 6, 8, 6, 7, 6 cm. Which record keeps ALL the information?

options.label: 6, 8, 6, 7, 6 — every measurement, repeats included
options.feedback: Correct — a record's job is completeness; the three 6s are three real ribbons, not one.

options.label: 6, 7, 8 — just the different values
options.feedback: Dropping repeats erases HOW MANY ribbons hit each length — the very thing a line plot will need.

options.label: The biggest: 8
options.feedback: One number describes one ribbon; four others vanish from that record.

options.label: About 7 each
options.feedback: An average-flavored summary trades away the individual measurements a plot is built from.

hints: Mark to mark is the length.

widget.prompt: A ribbon in the group stretches from the 2 cm mark to the 11 cm mark. How long is it?

commonErrors.feedback: That read the end mark as the length — subtract where the ribbon starts.
Adding the marks measures nothing; the span between them is the length.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Read the display itself: count what is drawn, and let the stacks, rows, and bars do the remembering.
